key_insight: Measurement incompatibility can survive mathematically but become operationally hidden after a quantum channel, and the paper formalizes when and how that concealment occurs.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum engineers a way to analyze whether restricted readout or noisy channels erase accessible incompatibility, which matters for sensing, certification, and semi-device-independent protocols.
method: Build an adjoint-kernel framework to group observables into operational equivalence classes.
Define concealment robustness and compute it via explicit SDP formulations.
Characterize concealment geometrically for unbiased binary qubit POVMs under rank-2 unital qubit channels.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical classification results and explicit families showing that concealment robustness matches incompatibility robustness for injective channels but can be strictly smaller for non-injective channels.
watch_item: The framework is most directly applicable to structured channel classes and qubit POVMs, so general high-dimensional or strongly non-unital settings may require additional analysis.
paper_title: Operational Concealment of Measurement Incompatibility by Quantum Channels
